stage1.impression: A quiet, believable composition: the red acrylic cabinet glows and is clearly the hero, and the record wall gives the room a warm, lived-in edge. But the light is one even, milky veil with no pools. Walls, artwork and shelves all sit at the same mid-brown, the blacks are lifted, the wall panel reads as a dim print rather than a back-lit frosted screen, and at 1:1 the concrete reads as smooth plaster and the record spines as a repeated pattern, so it still looks like a competent CG proof rather than a night photograph.

blocking_9: Distinct pools of light (record wall, side table, speaker) with real dark between them: wall and shelf regions need a lum_range above about 90, not 20 to 70
Shadows deep but clean: frame lum_p5 at or below about 7, not a lifted 12 caused by haze and a flat tone curve
The frosted screen panel must read as a glowing, evenly diffused back-lit panel, not as a framed print on the wall
Board-formed concrete has to read at 1:1, with board grain, pour lines and tie holes; it currently reads as smooth plaster
Some sign of life: a glass on the side table, a record out of its sleeve, a coat
The fir beams overhead and the chairs turned toward the speaker, which the card says the frame is for, are not in the shot (one chair only, no beams)
Judged at full resolution (this proof is 720 x 480, scale 0.3); nothing at this size can show the material detail a 9 needs

defects.what: Frosted screen panel has median luminance 38.5 and a range of 21.5, the same as the wall around it. It reads as a dull framed print, not glowing acrylic
Concrete wall is flat: lum_range 20, smooth plaster-like, with no visible formwork grain or pools of light
Record wall is evenly lit with no spot pools (y profile 45/42/44/47/36/30/34/35). The record spines repeat as a CG texture pattern
Leather chair is a near-featureless dark mass (median 14.7, p95 53) filling a quarter of the frame. There is no rim light and no leather sheen
Table lamp dome reads near-white and pinkish (median 166) rather than smoked, yet throws only a small pool on the table (table p95 86)
Global milky veil: lum_p5 12.1 and no true blacks, from the haze and a flat AgX curve
Horn's top face is dark and muddy apart from one hard white specular streak at the left edge, which looks like a plastic highlight
Floor barely reads: no polish, no reflection of the speaker's red glow, so the speaker's plinth floats
Lower fir cabinet doors are uniform, smooth and dark, with no grain contrast or edge highlights

changes.problem: The record wall has no pools of light: it is lit as evenly as the wall, so the room reads as flatly lit CG.

change.setting: the record wall 3 x spot, W
change.to: 80.0 W, cone 22 deg, aimed at the upper three shelf rows so each throws a scalloped pool that falls off down the wall

changes.expected: Bright pools on the record spines (p95 about 140) with falloff to dark below, and visible scallops on the shelf faces

changes.problem: Haze lays a uniform veil over the frame that lifts every shadow to the same grey-brown and removes the dark between the pools.

change.setting: haze in the room's air, density per metre

changes.expected: Deeper, cleaner shadows. Haze shows only in the cones of the spots and around the speaker, not across the wall

changes.problem: The frosted screen panel does not glow. It reads as a framed print, so the room's back-lit acrylic idea is lost.

evidence.measured: lum_median 38.5, lum_range 21.5, equal to the surrounding wall (37.7)

changes.expected: The panel glows softly and evenly, about twice the brightness of the wall, with the dark form inside it still diffuse and soft

changes.problem: The tone curve is flat: mids and shadows sit within a narrow band, so nothing has depth.

change.to: AgX - Medium High Contrast (exposure 0.0 kept; re-check the median after c1 to c3)

changes.expected: Frame median stays about 30 to 40 while p95 rises and p5 falls: a low-key frame with real blacks

changes.problem: The speaker as a whole falls below the readability bar: its horn top is muddy except for one hard white streak.

evidence.measured: lum_median 36.7 (target 45 or more); cabinet body alone 47.3; horn top dark with a single specular streak

change.setting: on each Ember speaker 4 x area, W/m2
change.to: 15.0 W/m2, with the upper lamp enlarged or moved so the horn gets a broad soft reflection, not a thin streak

changes.expected: Horn and cabinet both legible, with red light carried through the acrylic and a broad soft highlight on the horn

changes.problem: The table lamp dome reads as white plastic rather than smoked acrylic, while the light it throws on the table and chair is weak.

change.setting: EARF Moon: the lamp in each table lamp / frosted domes' own glow

changes.expected: The dome darkens and reads as smoked with a bright rim. A clear warm pool forms on the side-table top and catches the chair's leather arm

changes.problem: At 1:1 the concrete reads as smooth plaster, and the fir doors as flat dark veneer.

evidence.measured: wall lum_range 20.2, p5 to p95 23 to 43; no board grain or tie holes visible in the crop

change.setting: concrete finish (tone, sheen, bump); fir stain
change.to: board-grain bump strength about 2 to 3 times higher, horizontal pour lines, visible tie holes, slight sheen; fir doors with a lighter stain so the grain shows

changes.expected: Concrete shows formwork boards under the grazing light from the speaker and the record-wall spots

changes.problem: The room has no sign of life, and the dark chair back dominates the lower left.

evidence.measured: chair median 14.7, a featureless mass covering about 24% of the frame; only a candle on the table

change.from: an empty side table, one chair seen from behind
change.to: a rocks glass with whisky beside the lamp, a record out of its sleeve leaning on the cabinet base, a coat over the chair arm; camera yawed about 5 deg right and lowered to a seated 1.05 m so the chair crops less and a second chair turned to the speaker enters

changes.expected: A lived-in frame with small highlights on the glass and the vinyl; the chair becomes framing rather than a void

out_of_scope.request: Make the EARF Moon dome itself darker or more smoked in its material
out_of_scope.why: The EARF product's colour and parts are fixed; only its light levels can change (handled in c6)

out_of_scope.request: Soften the speaker's saturated red tint toward a less signage-like red
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's colour is fixed by the card
The camera must stay level, and the beams sit above this frame. Showing them needs a wider lens or a different camera position, which the owner should choose against the listening-room brief
